# What Polar organization access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, which no real credential is. That run is
# thirty-six characters and a body is forty-three, so a body is the run and
# seven characters of it again, and the ten character prefix in front brings a
# token to fifty-three. Where the case is what a case is about the same run is
# written in capitals, since base62 holds the letters of both. The one case the
# run cannot state is the body of a single repeated character, which is what
# shows that the checksum is read as a width and not verified; it carries no run
# at all.

patterns: polar-organization-access-token

# The prefix Polar writes an organization access token with, in the places a
# token is written: the environment a server reads it from, the header the API
# reference writes a request with, and the configuration a framework adapter
# takes it in.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=«polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a token in the authorization header a request carries
in:       Authorization: Bearer polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      Authorization: Bearer «polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a token in the configuration an sdk is constructed with
in:       {"accessToken":"polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456"}
out:      {"accessToken":"«polar-organization-access-token»"}

case:     a token between tabs
in:       field\tpolar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456\tnext
out:      field\t«polar-organization-access-token»\tnext

case:     a token followed by crlf
in:       POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456\r\n
out:      POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=«polar-organization-access-token»\r\n

# The alphabet the forty-three characters are written in: base62, which is the
# letters of both cases and the digits. What it leaves out is the hyphen and the
# underscore base64url adds, so a body carrying either is no body — and the
# underscore is what ends a body at the next segment of a snake_case name. The
# prefix is read in lowercase alone, since the uppercase spelling is the shape
# an environment variable's name is written in.

case:     a body of uppercase letters
in:       polar_oat_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a hyphen in the body
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghij-lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     an underscore in the body
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghij_lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       POLAR_OAT_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      POLAR_OAT_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     hyphens where the prefix carries its underscores
in:       polar-oat-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      polar-oat-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     the kind with one letter capitalized
in:       polar_Oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      polar_Oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

# The lengths either side of forty-three. Polar's own generator writes every
# token at the one width — thirty-seven characters drawn from the letters and
# the digits, and six more of a base62 checksum over them — so the count is read
# as a count rather than a floor: forty-two characters are not a token, and
# forty-four are a token and one character that belongs to no credential. The
# second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the match — a
# boundary there would drop this token rather than trim it, and a real token
# written against a character of the alphabet would come through whole.

case:     a body of forty-three characters is a token
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a body of forty-two characters is not
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345
out:      polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345

case:     an alphabet run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234567
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»7

# The checksum is read as six characters of the alphabet and not verified. Every
# body here fails it — the ordered run is no checksum of itself — and every one
# of them is redacted, which is what a caller wants of a token mistyped into a
# ticket or rewritten by an editor that took it for a word.

case:     a body of one repeated character
in:       polar_oat_zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN_polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN_«polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xpolar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      x«polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456-suffix
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»-suffix

case:     a token before a snake_case word
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456_suffix
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»_suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456.
out:      the token is «polar-organization-access-token».

case:     a token between multi-byte text with nothing between them
in:       日本語polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456日本語
out:      日本語«polar-organization-access-token»日本語

# Two tokens written together. A token can begin inside another, in the last
# five characters of a body: the five letters the prefix opens with are letters
# a body may hold and the underscore behind them is not, so an opening inside a
# token needs that underscore to fall past the token's end. The two spans
# overlap there and the whole of it is redacted as one. Written without that
# overlap the two are separate values and both go. The five positions are
# written out one by one in the pattern's own test file; here are the furthest
# and the nearest of them, and the opening one character further in, which is
# what bounds the five — the underscore that opening needs falls where a body
# would have to carry one, so what stands there is a token and the text in front
# of it rather than two tokens overlapping.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»«polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a token beginning five characters from the end of another
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a token beginning at the last character of another
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «polar-organization-access-token»

case:     an opening one character further in than the five reach
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0«polar-organization-access-token»

case:     a prefix written where a body would stand
in:       polar_oat_polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      polar_oat_«polar-organization-access-token»

case:     two different tokens on one line separated by a space
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456 polar_oat_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456
out:      «polar-organization-access-token» «polar-organization-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix is ten characters of
# an alphabet of sixty-four, so a base64url payload long enough to spell it
# carries a candidate, and where the forty-three behind it hold neither the
# hyphen nor the underscore they are a body. That is the answer rather than a
# fault in it, because sparing it would spare a real token: the vendor's format
# is that prefix and that many of those characters, and no part of it is left
# for such a run to fail. Standard base64 and hexadecimal write no underscore at
# all, so neither carries a candidate at however long it runs.

case:     the prefix inside a longer base64url run
in:       payload=zzzzpolar_oat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456zzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«polar-organization-access-token»zzzz

case:     a standard base64 payload, which carries no underscore
in:       payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEApolaroat0123456789abcdef
out:      payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEApolaroat0123456789abcdef

case:     a hexadecimal digest, which carries no underscore either
in:       digest=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      digest=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first two are prefixes Polar writes
# behind the same generator, which the pattern's own file weighs and declines to
# read: every credential Polar issues is that generator's forty-three characters
# behind a prefix of its own, so what tells one from another is the prefix
# alone, and each is a credential of its own rather than a width this pattern is
# missing. Then a body a space has broken, and two inputs carrying no prefix at
# all: a run of the right length opening with something else, and a line of
# prose, which holds nothing as long as a body and no run unbroken by a space.

case:     a personal access token, which is a credential of its own
in:       POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=polar_pat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=polar_pat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     an oauth access token, which is a credential of its own
in:       Authorization: Bearer polar_at_o_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      Authorization: Bearer polar_at_o_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      polar_oat_0123456789abcdefghij lmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxxx_xxx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      xxxxx_xxx_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="creating a checkout" organization_id=1dbfc517 url=https://api.polar.sh/v1/checkouts
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="creating a checkout" organization_id=1dbfc517 url=https://api.polar.sh/v1/checkouts
